## Premise

A broken Guild wagon blocks a forest crossing. Keep its driver safe while hungry Rifthounds close in.

Tone: Urgent, practical, hopeful survival

A quick defence with a clear rescue objective, useful terrain and one fight.

## Private truths and reveal conditions

## The stalled crossing

Get the people and essential cargo away from a predator at the damaged wagon.

Character entry and scope. Recommended level 1–3; one player with zero to 2 optional companions. This is guidance, not an enforced level limit. The chosen character can accept the immediate invitation, negotiate terms or decline. Establish any needed local context openly without inventing prior player actions.

Nessa Rill, Guild driver: capable, embarrassed and direct. She wants everyone alive, then the medicine saved. She offers 10 gp for assistance and will give up the flour without an argument. She can explain the broken axle immediately; no persuasion roll is required.

Orlo, a porter sheltering behind a stone, wants to retrieve a dropped keepsake. He follows a clear safe instruction and can carry the medicine. He is a person to protect, not a compulsory combat companion.

Ground. The cart is ten feet long with a five-foot gap on either side between its wheels and the clearing stones. Its body gives ordinary cover when the geometry supports it. The ditch is difficult footing but conceals someone carrying a small load. A loose flour sack lies near the animal’s approach; splitting it distracts with scent and dust rather than causing magical blindness.

Information. Nessa points out that the animal keeps sniffing the flour. Following its gaze reveals the spilled provisions without a check. The replacement pin fits, but the wheel must be lifted. A player can hold off the animal, help repair, carry the medicine out, bait it away or propose a different escape.

Repair. Nessa needs two uninterrupted opportunities to work after someone steadies the wheel. A character using their action to help completes one opportunity with her; a suitable tool or lever can remove the need to hold it. An attack forcing her away interrupts that opportunity, not earlier work. Count this openly as GM-adjudicated progress. Do not make it an invisible timer or grant extra combat actions.

People before property. If the player abandons the cart, Nessa can lead Orlo along the ditch while the player covers the retreat. The animal pursues accessible food rather than inexplicably hunting fleeing people. If no one helps, Nessa offers the flour and attempts that escape herself.

### Objectives

objective-1

### Approaches and branches

Bait with provisions: surrender the flour, move the people and medicine while the beast feeds, and resolve any uncertain close approach with the Ruleset.

Hold and repair: defend the wagon long enough to restore the wheel, then leave together.

Leave the load: carry only what is safe. Orlo’s keepsake can be recovered if the situation permits; losing it is a small personal cost, not a second quest.

### Consequences

Record whether Nessa, Orlo, the medicine and flour escape. Nessa pays the agreed amount if able; partial recovery earns gratitude even if the job loses money.

If the player made a promise to Orlo, resolve it in the aftermath. A saved keepsake becomes a tangible thank-you rather than an automatic companion recruitment.

All linked objective conditions are required, including the named closing event. Carry optional promises forward; they neither replace nor extend this ending.

### Prepared encounters

One encounter only. Solo level-one baseline: a hungry juvenile Rifthound, AC 12, HP 9, speed 40 ft, initiative +2; bite +3 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target, 1d4+1 piercing. This is an authored weaker adaptation of the referenced creature. It has no phase-step, regeneration, resistances or multiattack. Use start_combat_encounter_entities if combat begins, then resolve_adjudicated_creature_attack for its bite with these declared inputs. The first lunge targets exposed food or whoever blocks access. It retreats at 3 HP or when it can carry food clear. For a higher-level character or multiple combatants, choose and disclose an appropriate number or stronger referenced version before engagement; preserve the one encounter and objective instead of spawning surprise waves.

Read the selected party before committing opposition. The written encounter is a suggested baseline, not automatic level scaling. Resolve checks, attacks, damage, resources and combat turns through the admitted D&D SRD Ruleset; narrate only committed results. Preserve negotiation, surrender, retreat and established positions.

## The stalled crossing

Get the people and essential cargo away from a predator at the damaged wagon.

Character entry and scope. Recommended level 1–3; one player with zero to 2 optional companions. This is guidance, not an enforced level limit. The chosen character can accept the immediate invitation, negotiate terms or decline. Establish any needed local context openly without inventing prior player actions.

Nessa Rill, Guild driver: capable, embarrassed and direct. She wants everyone alive, then the medicine saved. She offers 10 gp for assistance and will give up the flour without an argument. She can explain the broken axle immediately; no persuasion roll is required.

Orlo, a porter sheltering behind a stone, wants to retrieve a dropped keepsake. He follows a clear safe instruction and can carry the medicine. He is a person to protect, not a compulsory combat companion.

Ground. The cart is ten feet long with a five-foot gap on either side between its wheels and the clearing stones. Its body gives ordinary cover when the geometry supports it. The ditch is difficult footing but conceals someone carrying a small load. A loose flour sack lies near the animal’s approach; splitting it distracts with scent and dust rather than causing magical blindness.

Information. Nessa points out that the animal keeps sniffing the flour. Following its gaze reveals the spilled provisions without a check. The replacement pin fits, but the wheel must be lifted. A player can hold off the animal, help repair, carry the medicine out, bait it away or propose a different escape.

## Premise

A broken Guild wagon blocks a forest crossing. Keep its driver safe while hungry Rifthounds close in.

Tone: Urgent, practical, hopeful survival

## Private truths and reveal conditions

## The stalled crossing

Get the people and essential cargo away from a predator at the damaged wagon.

Character entry and scope. Recommended level 1–3; one player with zero to 2 optional companions. This is guidance, not an enforced level limit. The chosen character can accept the immediate invitation, negotiate terms or decline. Establish any needed local context openly without inventing prior player actions.

Nessa Rill, Guild driver: capable, embarrassed and direct. She wants everyone alive, then the medicine saved. She offers 10 gp for assistance and will give up the flour without an argument. She can explain the broken axle immediately; no persuasion roll is required.

Orlo, a porter sheltering behind a stone, wants to retrieve a dropped keepsake. He follows a clear safe instruction and can carry the medicine. He is a person to protect, not a compulsory combat companion.

Ground. The cart is ten feet long with a five-foot gap on either side between its wheels and the clearing stones. Its body gives ordinary cover when the geometry supports it. The ditch is difficult footing but conceals someone carrying a small load. A loose flour sack lies near the animal’s approach; splitting it distracts with scent and dust rather than causing magical blindness.

Information. Nessa points out that the animal keeps sniffing the flour. Following its gaze reveals the spilled provisions without a check. The replacement pin fits, but the wheel must be lifted. A player can hold off the animal, help repair, carry the medicine out, bait it away or propose a different escape.

Repair. Nessa needs two uninterrupted opportunities to work after someone steadies the wheel. A character using their action to help completes one opportunity with her; a suitable tool or lever can remove the need to hold it. An attack forcing her away interrupts that opportunity, not earlier work. Count this openly as GM-adjudicated progress. Do not make it an invisible timer or grant extra combat actions.

People before property. If the player abandons the cart, Nessa can lead Orlo along the ditch while the player covers the retreat. The animal pursues accessible food rather than inexplicably hunting fleeing people. If no one helps, Nessa offers the flour and attempts that escape herself.

### Objectives

objective-1

### Approaches and branches

Bait with provisions: surrender the flour, move the people and medicine while the beast feeds, and resolve any uncertain close approach with the Ruleset.

Hold and repair: defend the wagon long enough to restore the wheel, then leave together.

Leave the load: carry only what is safe. Orlo’s keepsake can be recovered if the situation permits; losing it is a small personal cost, not a second quest.

### Consequences

Record whether Nessa, Orlo, the medicine and flour escape. Nessa pays the agreed amount if able; partial recovery earns gratitude even if the job loses money.

If the player made a promise to Orlo, resolve it in the aftermath. A saved keepsake becomes a tangible thank-you rather than an automatic companion recruitment.

All linked objective conditions are required, including the named closing event. Carry optional promises forward; they neither replace nor extend this ending.

### Prepared encounters

One encounter only. Solo level-one baseline: a hungry juvenile Rifthound, AC 12, HP 9, speed 40 ft, initiative +2; bite +3 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target, 1d4+1 piercing. This is an authored weaker adaptation of the referenced creature. It has no phase-step, regeneration, resistances or multiattack. Use start_combat_encounter_entities if combat begins, then resolve_adjudicated_creature_attack for its bite with these declared inputs. The first lunge targets exposed food or whoever blocks access. It retreats at 3 HP or when it can carry food clear. For a higher-level character or multiple combatants, choose and disclose an appropriate number or stronger referenced version before engagement; preserve the one encounter and objective instead of spawning surprise waves.

Read the selected party before committing opposition. The written encounter is a suggested baseline, not automatic level scaling. Resolve checks, attacks, damage, resources and combat turns through the admitted D&D SRD Ruleset; narrate only committed results. Preserve negotiation, surrender, retreat and established positions.

## Private truths and reveal conditions

## The stalled crossing

Get the people and essential cargo away from a predator at the damaged wagon.

Character entry and scope. Recommended level 1–3; one player with zero to 2 optional companions. This is guidance, not an enforced level limit. The chosen character can accept the immediate invitation, negotiate terms or decline. Establish any needed local context openly without inventing prior player actions.

Nessa Rill, Guild driver: capable, embarrassed and direct. She wants everyone alive, then the medicine saved. She offers 10 gp for assistance and will give up the flour without an argument. She can explain the broken axle immediately; no persuasion roll is required.

Orlo, a porter sheltering behind a stone, wants to retrieve a dropped keepsake. He follows a clear safe instruction and can carry the medicine. He is a person to protect, not a compulsory combat companion.

Information. Nessa points out that the animal keeps sniffing the flour. Following its gaze reveals the spilled provisions without a check. The replacement pin fits, but the wheel must be lifted. A player can hold off the animal, help repair, carry the medicine out, bait it away or propose a different escape.

Repair. Nessa needs two uninterrupted opportunities to work after someone steadies the wheel. A character using their action to help completes one opportunity with her; a suitable tool or lever can remove the need to hold it. objective-1

### Approaches and branches

Bait with provisions: surrender the flour, move the people and medicine while the beast feeds, and resolve any uncertain close approach with the Ruleset.

Hold and repair: defend the wagon long enough to restore the wheel, then leave together.

Leave the load: carry only what is safe. Orlo’s keepsake can be recovered if the situation permits; losing it is a small personal cost, not a second quest.

### Consequences

Record whether Nessa, Orlo, the medicine and flour escape. Nessa pays the agreed amount if able; partial recovery earns gratitude even if the job loses money.

If the player made a promise to Orlo, resolve it in the aftermath. A saved keepsake becomes a tangible thank-you rather than an automatic companion recruitment.

All linked objective conditions are required, including the named closing event. Carry optional promises forward; they neither replace nor extend this ending.

### Prepared encounters

One encounter only. Solo level-one baseline: a hungry juvenile Rifthound, AC 12, HP 9, speed 40 ft, initiative +2; bite +3 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target, 1d4+1 piercing. This is an authored weaker adaptation of the referenced creature. It has no phase-step, regeneration, resistances or multiattack. ## The stalled crossing

Get the people and essential cargo away from a predator at the damaged wagon.

Character entry and scope. Recommended level 1–3; one player with zero to 2 optional companions. This is guidance, not an enforced level limit. The chosen character can accept the immediate invitation, negotiate terms or decline. Establish any needed local context openly without inventing prior player actions.

Nessa Rill, Guild driver: capable, embarrassed and direct. She wants everyone alive, then the medicine saved. She offers 10 gp for assistance and will give up the flour without an argument. She can explain the broken axle immediately; no persuasion roll is required.

Orlo, a porter sheltering behind a stone, wants to retrieve a dropped keepsake. He follows a clear safe instruction and can carry the medicine. He is a person to protect, not a compulsory combat companion.

Ground. The cart is ten feet long with a five-foot gap on either side between its wheels and the clearing stones. Its body gives ordinary cover when the geometry supports it. The ditch is difficult footing but conceals someone carrying a small load. A loose flour sack lies near the animal’s approach; splitting it distracts with scent and dust rather than causing magical blindness.

Information. Nessa points out that the animal keeps sniffing the flour. Following its gaze reveals the spilled provisions without a check. The replacement pin fits, but the wheel must be lifted. A player can hold off the animal, help repair, carry the medicine out, bait it away or propose a different escape.

Repair. Nessa needs two uninterrupted opportunities to work after someone steadies the wheel. A character using their action to help completes one opportunity with her; a suitable tool or lever can remove the need to hold it. An attack forcing her away interrupts that opportunity, not earlier work. Count this openly as GM-adjudicated progress. Do not make it an invisible timer or grant extra combat actions.

People before property. If the player abandons the cart, Nessa can lead Orlo along the ditch while the player covers the retreat. The animal pursues accessible food rather than inexplicably hunting fleeing people. If no one helps, Nessa offers the flour and attempts that escape herself.

### Objectives

objective-1

### Approaches and branches

Bait with provisions: surrender the flour, move the people and medicine while the beast feeds, and resolve any uncertain close approach with the Ruleset.

Hold and repair: defend the wagon long enough to restore the wheel, then leave together.

Leave the load: carry only what is safe. Orlo’s keepsake can be recovered if the situation permits; losing it is a small personal cost, not a second quest.

### Consequences

Record whether Nessa, Orlo, the medicine and flour escape. Nessa pays the agreed amount if able; partial recovery earns gratitude even if the job loses money.

If the player made a promise to Orlo, resolve it in the aftermath. A saved keepsake becomes a tangible thank-you rather than an automatic companion recruitment.

# Last Cart Through

> GM preparation: contains adventure spoilers.

## Premise

A broken Guild wagon blocks a forest crossing. Keep its driver safe while hungry Rifthounds close in.

Tone: Urgent, practical, hopeful survival

A quick defence with a clear rescue objective, useful terrain and one fight.

## Character entry

```json

  "custom_companions": {
    "maximum": 2,
    "minimum": 0
  },
  "player_character": {

  },
  "required_companions": []
}
```

## Boundaries

Apply the player’s selected content boundaries; offer a less intense presentation where needed.

## Starting location

```json
{
  "id": "verdant-margin",
  "path": "locations/verdant-margin.md"
}
```

## Opening direction

Orient the player beside the disabled wagon. Show the driver, stable ground and approaching animals before asking what they do. The fight has not started.

## Starting facts and state

  "entities": [],
  "facts": [
    {
      "fact": "The selected party is beside a stranded wagon at a Verdant Margin Anchor Clearing. A cracked axle has left one wheel tilted into the growth.",
      "id": "opening-1",
      "known_by": [
        "player"
      ]
    },
    {
      "fact": "Driver Nessa Rill stands behind the wagon with a replacement pin and hammer. One lean juvenile Rifthound watches from the treeline, thirty feet away. No attack has occurred.",
      "id": "opening-2",
      "known_by": [
        "player"
      ]
    },
    {
      "fact": "The clearing remains stable. The wagon carries flour and a crate of medicine; a dry ditch leads to another patch of open ground.",
      "id": "opening-3",
      "known_by": [
        "player"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "mechanics": [
    {
      "key": "state",
      "namespace": "sylvia.srd-lite.bg3",
      "value": {
        "advancement": {
          "allocation": "The Player Character and Companions start and remain at level 2. Story success, defeat, combat and optional jobs never award advancement. Grant only the adventure's actually earned money, possessions and narrative rewards. Any lower-level encounter-variant notes are authoring guidance for a separately revised Plan, not permission to override this declaration in play.",
          "maximum_level": 2,
          "method": "fixed",
          "recipients": "whole_party",
          "starting_level": 2,
          "timing": "This edition stays at level 2 throughout its authored adventure and optional continuation. It awards no XP or level increases; changing that policy requires an explicitly revised Plan."
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

## Private truths and reveal conditions

## The stalled crossing

Get the people and essential cargo away from a predator at the damaged wagon.

Character entry and scope. Recommended level 1–3; one player with zero to 2 optional companions. This is guidance, not an enforced level limit. The chosen character can accept the immediate invitation, negotiate terms or decline. Establish any needed local context openly without inventing prior player actions.

Nessa Rill, Guild driver: capable, embarrassed and direct. She wants everyone alive, then the medicine saved. She offers 10 gp for assistance and will give up the flour without an argument. She can explain the broken axle immediately; no persuasion roll is required.

Orlo, a porter sheltering behind a stone, wants to retrieve a dropped keepsake. He follows a clear safe instruction and can carry the medicine. He is a person to protect, not a compulsory combat companion.

Ground. The cart is ten feet long with a five-foot gap on either side between its wheels and the clearing stones. Its body gives ordinary cover when the geometry supports it. The ditch is difficult footing but conceals someone carrying a small load. A loose flour sack lies near the animal’s approach; splitting it distracts with scent and dust rather than causing magical blindness.

Information. Nessa points out that the animal keeps sniffing the flour. Following its gaze reveals the spilled provisions without a check. The replacement pin fits, but the wheel must be lifted. A player can hold off the animal, help repair, carry the medicine out, bait it away or propose a different escape.

Repair. Nessa needs two uninterrupted opportunities to work after someone steadies the wheel. A character using their action to help completes one opportunity with her; a suitable tool or lever can remove the need to hold it. An attack forcing her away interrupts that opportunity, not earlier work. Count this openly as GM-adjudicated progress. Do not make it an invisible timer or grant extra combat actions.

People before property. If the player abandons the cart, Nessa can lead Orlo along the ditch while the player covers the retreat. The animal pursues accessible food rather than inexplicably hunting fleeing people. If no one helps, Nessa offers the flour and attempts that escape herself.

### Objectives

objective-1

### Approaches and branches

Bait with provisions: surrender the flour, move the people and medicine while the beast feeds, and resolve any uncertain close approach with the Ruleset.

Hold and repair: defend the wagon long enough to restore the wheel, then leave together.

Leave the load: carry only what is safe. Orlo’s keepsake can be recovered if the situation permits; losing it is a small personal cost, not a second quest.

### Consequences

Record whether Nessa, Orlo, the medicine and flour escape. Nessa pays the agreed amount if able; partial recovery earns gratitude even if the job loses money.

If the player made a promise to Orlo, resolve it in the aftermath. A saved keepsake becomes a tangible thank-you rather than an automatic companion recruitment.

All linked objective conditions are required, including the named closing event. Carry optional promises forward; they neither replace nor extend this ending.

### Prepared encounters

One encounter only. Solo level-one baseline: a hungry juvenile Rifthound, AC 12, HP 9, speed 40 ft, initiative +2; bite +3 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target, 1d4+1 piercing. This is an authored weaker adaptation of the referenced creature. It has no phase-step, regeneration, resistances or multiattack. Use start_combat_encounter_entities if combat begins, then resolve_adjudicated_creature_attack for its bite with these declared inputs. The first lunge targets exposed food or whoever blocks access. It retreats at 3 HP or when it can carry food clear. For a higher-level character or multiple combatants, choose and disclose an appropriate number or stronger referenced version before engagement; preserve the one encounter and objective instead of spawning surprise waves.

### Encounter adjudication

Read the selected party before committing opposition. The written encounter is a suggested baseline, not automatic level scaling. Resolve checks, attacks, damage, resources and combat turns through the admitted D&D SRD Ruleset; narrate only committed results. Preserve negotiation, surrender, retreat and established positions.

## GM guidance

Use this Plan as private preparation within Severed Lands. Ground play in the accepted party and starting facts. The named new people and incidents belong to this adventure; existing Setting facts and earned consequences remain authoritative. Give the player concrete information for a first decision, follow their chosen approach, and keep private answers concealed until discovered.

Make the named main problem and its leads accessible. Read the current act and all linked objective conditions before framing its main quest and reassess when a required result occurs. All listed conditions and the closing event are required; explicit alternatives satisfy only their own condition. Optional scenes can be deferred without adding gates. A completed side job does not replace the main story. Do not fabricate success or mark unplayed later acts complete after an early departure.

Objectives express opportunities, not mandatory conduct. A refusal, changed allegiance or early discovery can change the route or end the job. Carry forward established consequences instead of restoring a preferred plot.

Read this preparation and its relevant Setting sources. Keep a concise record of named promises, discovered evidence, lost resources and NPC attitudes. The preparation contains the core answer and resolutions; incidental dialogue and connective description remain the GM’s work.

Conclude after the bounded problem and immediate aftermath are resolved. Offer a short epilogue choice; begin a further adventure only if the player asks to continue.

## Completion and aftermath

The predator has left or been stopped, or the party and surviving Nessa and Orlo have escaped by the ditch to safe ground. Account for either person lost through actual play; an intention to retreat is not an escape.

The medicine and flour are each recorded as carried out, left at the wagon, consumed or lost through play. Record the wagon and any keepsake actually recovered; rescuing property is not required after the people are safe.

Closing event: on safe ground Nessa responds to the actual rescue and losses and settles the agreed assistance payment if able. If she was lost, Orlo or the receiving Guild contact takes the report instead. No additional delivery adventure is required.

Use the explicit failed-attempt outcome and closing report in the current objective. An intention to withdraw, an unrelated side task or delegation alone does not satisfy it. An early departure leaves unplayed later objectives unfinished.

Resolve defeat, unconsciousness, death and recovery under the selected Ruleset and agreed boundaries; no scripted rescue cancels committed results.

# Last Cart Through

> GM preparation: contains adventure spoilers.

## Premise

A broken Guild wagon blocks a forest crossing. Keep its driver safe while hungry Rifthounds close in.

Tone: Urgent, practical, hopeful survival

A quick defence with a clear rescue objective, useful terrain and one fight.

## Character entry

        }
      }
    }

```

## Private truths and reveal conditions

## The stalled crossing

Get the people and essential cargo away from a predator at the damaged wagon.

Character entry and scope. Recommended level 1–3; one player with zero to 2 optional companions. This is guidance, not an enforced level limit. The chosen character can accept the immediate invitation, negotiate terms or decline. Establish any needed local context openly without inventing prior player actions.

Nessa Rill, Guild driver: capable, embarrassed and direct. She wants everyone alive, then the medicine saved. She offers 10 gp for assistance and will give up the flour without an argument. She can explain the broken axle immediately; no persuasion roll is required.

Orlo, a porter sheltering behind a stone, wants to retrieve a dropped keepsake. He follows a clear safe instruction and can carry the medicine. He is a person to protect, not a compulsory combat companion.

Ground. The cart is ten feet long with a five-foot gap on either side between its wheels and the clearing stones. Its body gives ordinary cover when the geometry supports it. The ditch is difficult footing but conceals someone carrying a small load. A loose flour sack lies near the animal’s approach; splitting it distracts with scent and dust rather than causing magical blindness.

Information. Nessa points out that the animal keeps sniffing the flour. Following its gaze reveals the spilled provisions without a check. The replacement pin fits, but the wheel must be lifted. A player can hold off the animal, help repair, carry the medicine out, bait it away or propose a different escape.

Repair. Nessa needs two uninterrupted opportunities to work after someone steadies the wheel. A character using their action to help completes one opportunity with her; a suitable tool or lever can remove the need to hold it. An attack forcing her away interrupts that opportunity, not earlier work. Count this openly as GM-adjudicated progress. Do not make it an invisible timer or grant extra combat actions.

People before property. If the player abandons the cart, Nessa can lead Orlo along the ditch while the player covers the retreat. The animal pursues accessible food rather than inexplicably hunting fleeing people. If no one helps, Nessa offers the flour and attempts that escape herself.

### Objectives

objective-1

### Approaches and branches

Bait with provisions: surrender the flour, move the people and medicine while the beast feeds, and resolve any uncertain close approach with the Ruleset.

Hold and repair: defend the wagon long enough to restore the wheel, then leave together.

Leave the load: carry only what is safe. Orlo’s keepsake can be recovered if the situation permits; losing it is a small personal cost, not a second quest.

### Consequences

Record whether Nessa, Orlo, the medicine and flour escape. Nessa pays the agreed amount if able; partial recovery earns gratitude even if the job loses money.

If the player made a promise to Orlo, resolve it in the aftermath. A saved keepsake becomes a tangible thank-you rather than an automatic companion recruitment.

All linked objective conditions are required, including the named closing event. Carry optional promises forward; they neither replace nor extend this ending.

### Prepared encounters

One encounter only. Solo level-one baseline: a hungry juvenile Rifthound, AC 12, HP 9, speed 40 ft, initiative +2; bite +3 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target, 1d4+1 piercing. This is an authored weaker adaptation of the referenced creature. It has no phase-step, regeneration, resistances or multiattack. Use start_combat_encounter_entities if combat begins, then resolve_adjudicated_creature_attack for its bite with these declared inputs. The first lunge targets exposed food or whoever blocks access. It retreats at 3 HP or when it can carry food clear. Read the selected party before committing opposition. The written encounter is a suggested baseline, not automatic level scaling. ## The stalled crossing

Get the people and essential cargo away from a predator at the damaged wagon.

Character entry and scope. Recommended level 1–3; one player with zero to 2 optional companions. This is guidance, not an enforced level limit. The chosen character can accept the immediate invitation, negotiate terms or decline. Establish any needed local context openly without inventing prior player actions.

Nessa Rill, Guild driver: capable, embarrassed and direct. She wants everyone alive, then the medicine saved. She offers 10 gp for assistance and will give up the flour without an argument. She can explain the broken axle immediately; no persuasion roll is required.

Orlo, a porter sheltering behind a stone, wants to retrieve a dropped keepsake. He follows a clear safe instruction and can carry the medicine. He is a person to protect, not a compulsory combat companion.

Ground. The cart is ten feet long with a five-foot gap on either side between its wheels and the clearing stones. Its body gives ordinary cover when the geometry supports it. The ditch is difficult footing but conceals someone carrying a small load. A loose flour sack lies near the animal’s approach; splitting it distracts with scent and dust rather than causing magical blindness.

Information. Nessa points out that the animal keeps sniffing the flour. Following its gaze reveals the spilled provisions without a check. The replacement pin fits, but the wheel must be lifted. A player can hold off the animal, help repair, carry the medicine out, bait it away or propose a different escape.

Repair. Nessa needs two uninterrupted opportunities to work after someone steadies the wheel. A character using their action to help completes one opportunity with her; a suitable tool or lever can remove the need to hold it. An attack forcing her away interrupts that opportunity, not earlier work. Count this openly as GM-adjudicated progress. Do not make it an invisible timer or grant extra combat actions.

People before property. If the player abandons the cart, Nessa can lead Orlo along the ditch while the player covers the retreat. The animal pursues accessible food rather than inexplicably hunting fleeing people. If no one helps, Nessa offers the flour and attempts that escape herself.

A broken Guild wagon blocks a forest crossing. Keep its driver safe while hungry Rifthounds close in.

Tone: Urgent, practical, hopeful survival

## Private truths and reveal conditions

## The stalled crossing

Get the people and essential cargo away from a predator at the damaged wagon.

Character entry and scope. Recommended level 1–3; one player with zero to 2 optional companions. This is guidance, not an enforced level limit. The chosen character can accept the immediate invitation, negotiate terms or decline. Establish any needed local context openly without inventing prior player actions.

Nessa Rill, Guild driver: capable, embarrassed and direct. She wants everyone alive, then the medicine saved. She offers 10 gp for assistance and will give up the flour without an argument. She can explain the broken axle immediately; no persuasion roll is required.

Orlo, a porter sheltering behind a stone, wants to retrieve a dropped keepsake. He follows a clear safe instruction and can carry the medicine. He is a person to protect, not a compulsory combat companion.

Ground. The cart is ten feet long with a five-foot gap on either side between its wheels and the clearing stones. Its body gives ordinary cover when the geometry supports it. The ditch is difficult footing but conceals someone carrying a small load. A loose flour sack lies near the animal’s approach; splitting it distracts with scent and dust rather than causing magical blindness.

Information. Nessa points out that the animal keeps sniffing the flour. Following its gaze reveals the spilled provisions without a check. The replacement pin fits, but the wheel must be lifted. A player can hold off the animal, help repair, carry the medicine out, bait it away or propose a different escape.

Repair. Nessa needs two uninterrupted opportunities to work after someone steadies the wheel. A character using their action to help completes one opportunity with her; a suitable tool or lever can remove the need to hold it. An attack forcing her away interrupts that opportunity, not earlier work. Count this openly as GM-adjudicated progress. Do not make it an invisible timer or grant extra combat actions.

People before property. If the player abandons the cart, Nessa can lead Orlo along the ditch while the player covers the retreat. The animal pursues accessible food rather than inexplicably hunting fleeing people. If no one helps, Nessa offers the flour and attempts that escape herself.

### Objectives

objective-1

### Approaches and branches

Bait with provisions: surrender the flour, move the people and medicine while the beast feeds, and resolve any uncertain close approach with the Ruleset.

Hold and repair: defend the wagon long enough to restore the wheel, then leave together.

Leave the load: carry only what is safe. Orlo’s keepsake can be recovered if the situation permits; losing it is a small personal cost, not a second quest.

### Consequences

Record whether Nessa, Orlo, the medicine and flour escape. Nessa pays the agreed amount if able; partial recovery earns gratitude even if the job loses money.

If the player made a promise to Orlo, resolve it in the aftermath. A saved keepsake becomes a tangible thank-you rather than an automatic companion recruitment.

All linked objective conditions are required, including the named closing event. Carry optional promises forward; they neither replace nor extend this ending.

### Prepared encounters

One encounter only. Solo level-one baseline: a hungry juvenile Rifthound, AC 12, HP 9, speed 40 ft, initiative +2; bite +3 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target, 1d4+1 piercing. This is an authored weaker adaptation of the referenced creature. It has no phase-step, regeneration, resistances or multiattack. Use start_combat_encounter_entities if combat begins, then resolve_adjudicated_creature_attack for its bite with these declared inputs. The first lunge targets exposed food or whoever blocks access. It retreats at 3 HP or when it can carry food clear. Observant and cheerful; prefers a useful question to a speech. No fixed home, allegiance, or campaign history is assigned.

Fight at range with a longbow. Hunter's Mark has two free uses per Long Rest; keep Concentration on the marked target.

# Last Cart Through

> GM preparation: contains adventure spoilers.

## Premise

A broken Guild wagon blocks a forest crossing. Keep its driver safe while hungry Rifthounds close in.

Tone: Urgent, practical, hopeful survival

A quick defence with a clear rescue objective, useful terrain and one fight.

## Character entry

```

## Private truths and reveal conditions

## The stalled crossing

Get the people and essential cargo away from a predator at the damaged wagon.

Character entry and scope. Recommended level 1–3; one player with zero to 2 optional companions. This is guidance, not an enforced level limit. The chosen character can accept the immediate invitation, negotiate terms or decline. Establish any needed local context openly without inventing prior player actions.

Nessa Rill, Guild driver: capable, embarrassed and direct. She wants everyone alive, then the medicine saved. She offers 10 gp for assistance and will give up the flour without an argument. She can explain the broken axle immediately; no persuasion roll is required.

Orlo, a porter sheltering behind a stone, wants to retrieve a dropped keepsake. He follows a clear safe instruction and can carry the medicine. He is a person to protect, not a compulsory combat companion.

Ground. The cart is ten feet long with a five-foot gap on either side between its wheels and the clearing stones. Its body gives ordinary cover when the geometry supports it. The ditch is difficult footing but conceals someone carrying a small load. A loose flour sack lies near the animal’s approach; splitting it distracts with scent and dust rather than causing magical blindness.

Information. Nessa points out that the animal keeps sniffing the flour. Following its gaze reveals the spilled provisions without a check. The replacement pin fits, but the wheel must be lifted. A player can hold off the animal, help repair, carry the medicine out, bait it away or propose a different escape.

Repair. Nessa needs two uninterrupted opportunities to work after someone steadies the wheel. A character using their action to help completes one opportunity with her; a suitable tool or lever can remove the need to hold it. An attack forcing her away interrupts that opportunity, not earlier work. Count this openly as GM-adjudicated progress. Do not make it an invisible timer or grant extra combat actions.

People before property. If the player abandons the cart, Nessa can lead Orlo along the ditch while the player covers the retreat. The animal pursues accessible food rather than inexplicably hunting fleeing people. If no one helps, Nessa offers the flour and attempts that escape herself.

### Objectives

objective-1

### Approaches and branches

Bait with provisions: surrender the flour, move the people and medicine while the beast feeds, and resolve any uncertain close approach with the Ruleset.

Hold and repair: defend the wagon long enough to restore the wheel, then leave together.

Leave the load: carry only what is safe. Orlo’s keepsake can be recovered if the situation permits; losing it is a small personal cost, not a second quest.

### Consequences

Record whether Nessa, Orlo, the medicine and flour escape. Nessa pays the agreed amount if able; partial recovery earns gratitude even if the job loses money.

If the player made a promise to Orlo, resolve it in the aftermath. A saved keepsake becomes a tangible thank-you rather than an automatic companion recruitment.

All linked objective conditions are required, including the named closing event. Carry optional promises forward; they neither replace nor extend this ending.

### Prepared encounters

One encounter only. Solo level-one baseline: a hungry juvenile Rifthound, AC 12, HP 9, speed 40 ft, initiative +2; bite +3 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target, 1d4+1 piercing. This is an authored weaker adaptation of the referenced creature. It has no phase-step, regeneration, resistances or multiattack. Use start_combat_encounter_entities if combat begins, then resolve_adjudicated_creature_attack for its bite with these declared inputs. The first lunge targets exposed food or whoever blocks access. It retreats at 3 HP or when it can carry food clear. For a higher-level character or multiple combatants, choose and disclose an appropriate number or stronger referenced version before engagement; preserve the one encounter and objective instead of spawning surprise waves.

Read the selected party before committing opposition. The written encounter is a suggested baseline, not automatic level scaling. Resolve checks, attacks, damage, resources and combat turns through the admitted D&D SRD Ruleset; narrate only committed results. Preserve negotiation, surrender, retreat and established positions.

> GM preparation: contains adventure spoilers.

## Premise

A broken Guild wagon blocks a forest crossing. Keep its driver safe while hungry Rifthounds close in.

Tone: Urgent, practical, hopeful survival

A quick defence with a clear rescue objective, useful terrain and one fight.

## Private truths and reveal conditions

## The stalled crossing

Get the people and essential cargo away from a predator at the damaged wagon.

Character entry and scope. Recommended level 1–3; one player with zero to 2 optional companions. This is guidance, not an enforced level limit. The chosen character can accept the immediate invitation, negotiate terms or decline. Establish any needed local context openly without inventing prior player actions.

Nessa Rill, Guild driver: capable, embarrassed and direct. She wants everyone alive, then the medicine saved. She offers 10 gp for assistance and will give up the flour without an argument. She can explain the broken axle immediately; no persuasion roll is required.

Orlo, a porter sheltering behind a stone, wants to retrieve a dropped keepsake. He follows a clear safe instruction and can carry the medicine. He is a person to protect, not a compulsory combat companion.

Ground. The cart is ten feet long with a five-foot gap on either side between its wheels and the clearing stones. Its body gives ordinary cover when the geometry supports it. The ditch is difficult footing but conceals someone carrying a small load. A loose flour sack lies near the animal’s approach; splitting it distracts with scent and dust rather than causing magical blindness.

Information. Nessa points out that the animal keeps sniffing the flour. Following its gaze reveals the spilled provisions without a check. The replacement pin fits, but the wheel must be lifted. A player can hold off the animal, help repair, carry the medicine out, bait it away or propose a different escape.

Repair. Nessa needs two uninterrupted opportunities to work after someone steadies the wheel. A character using their action to help completes one opportunity with her; a suitable tool or lever can remove the need to hold it. An attack forcing her away interrupts that opportunity, not earlier work. Count this openly as GM-adjudicated progress. Do not make it an invisible timer or grant extra combat actions.

People before property. If the player abandons the cart, Nessa can lead Orlo along the ditch while the player covers the retreat. The animal pursues accessible food rather than inexplicably hunting fleeing people. If no one helps, Nessa offers the flour and attempts that escape herself.

### Objectives

objective-1

### Approaches and branches

Bait with provisions: surrender the flour, move the people and medicine while the beast feeds, and resolve any uncertain close approach with the Ruleset.

Hold and repair: defend the wagon long enough to restore the wheel, then leave together.

Leave the load: carry only what is safe. Orlo’s keepsake can be recovered if the situation permits; losing it is a small personal cost, not a second quest.

### Consequences

Record whether Nessa, Orlo, the medicine and flour escape. Nessa pays the agreed amount if able; partial recovery earns gratitude even if the job loses money.

If the player made a promise to Orlo, resolve it in the aftermath. A saved keepsake becomes a tangible thank-you rather than an automatic companion recruitment.

All linked objective conditions are required, including the named closing event. Carry optional promises forward; they neither replace nor extend this ending.

### Prepared encounters

One encounter only. Solo level-one baseline: a hungry juvenile Rifthound, AC 12, HP 9, speed 40 ft, initiative +2; bite +3 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target, 1d4+1 piercing. This is an authored weaker adaptation of the referenced creature. It has no phase-step, regeneration, resistances or multiattack. Use start_combat_encounter_entities if combat begins, then resolve_adjudicated_creature_attack for its bite with these declared inputs. The first lunge targets exposed food or whoever blocks access. It retreats at 3 HP or when it can carry food clear. For a higher-level character or multiple combatants, choose and disclose an appropriate number or stronger referenced version before engagement; preserve the one encounter and objective instead of spawning surprise waves.

Read the selected party before committing opposition. The written encounter is a suggested baseline, not automatic level scaling. Resolve checks, attacks, damage, resources and combat turns through the admitted D&D SRD Ruleset; narrate only committed results. Preserve negotiation, surrender, retreat and established positions.

Get the people and essential cargo away from a predator at the damaged wagon.

Character entry and scope. Recommended level 1–3; one player with zero to 2 optional companions. This is guidance, not an enforced level limit. The chosen character can accept the immediate invitation, negotiate terms or decline. Establish any needed local context openly without inventing prior player actions.

Nessa Rill, Guild driver: capable, embarrassed and direct. She wants everyone alive, then the medicine saved. She offers 10 gp for assistance and will give up the flour without an argument. She can explain the broken axle immediately; no persuasion roll is required.

Orlo, a porter sheltering behind a stone, wants to retrieve a dropped keepsake. He follows a clear safe instruction and can carry the medicine. He is a person to protect, not a compulsory combat companion.

Ground. The cart is ten feet long with a five-foot gap on either side between its wheels and the clearing stones. Its body gives ordinary cover when the geometry supports it. The ditch is difficult footing but conceals someone carrying a small load. A loose flour sack lies near the animal’s approach; splitting it distracts with scent and dust rather than causing magical blindness.

Information. Nessa points out that the animal keeps sniffing the flour. Following its gaze reveals the spilled provisions without a check. The replacement pin fits, but the wheel must be lifted. A player can hold off the animal, help repair, carry the medicine out, bait it away or propose a different escape.

Repair. Nessa needs two uninterrupted opportunities to work after someone steadies the wheel. A character using their action to help completes one opportunity with her; a suitable tool or lever can remove the need to hold it. An attack forcing her away interrupts that opportunity, not earlier work. Count this openly as GM-adjudicated progress. Do not make it an invisible timer or grant extra combat actions.

People before property. If the player abandons the cart, Nessa can lead Orlo along the ditch while the player covers the retreat. The animal pursues accessible food rather than inexplicably hunting fleeing people. If no one helps, Nessa offers the flour and attempts that escape herself.

Bait with provisions: surrender the flour, move the people and medicine while the beast feeds, and resolve any uncertain close approach with the Ruleset.

Hold and repair: defend the wagon long enough to restore the wheel, then leave together.

Leave the load: carry only what is safe. Orlo’s keepsake can be recovered if the situation permits; losing it is a small personal cost, not a second quest.

### Consequences

Record whether Nessa, Orlo, the medicine and flour escape. Nessa pays the agreed amount if able; partial recovery earns gratitude even if the job loses money.

If the player made a promise to Orlo, resolve it in the aftermath. A saved keepsake becomes a tangible thank-you rather than an automatic companion recruitment.

All linked objective conditions are required, including the named closing event. Carry optional promises forward; they neither replace nor extend this ending.

One encounter only. Solo level-one baseline: a hungry juvenile Rifthound, AC 12, HP 9, speed 40 ft, initiative +2; bite +3 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target, 1d4+1 piercing. ## Premise

A broken Guild wagon blocks a forest crossing. Keep its driver safe while hungry Rifthounds close in.

Tone: Urgent, practical, hopeful survival

A quick defence with a clear rescue objective, useful terrain and one fight.

## Private truths and reveal conditions

## The stalled crossing

Get the people and essential cargo away from a predator at the damaged wagon.

Character entry and scope. Recommended level 1–3; one player with zero to 2 optional companions. This is guidance, not an enforced level limit. The chosen character can accept the immediate invitation, negotiate terms or decline. Establish any needed local context openly without inventing prior player actions.

Nessa Rill, Guild driver: capable, embarrassed and direct. She wants everyone alive, then the medicine saved. She offers 10 gp for assistance and will give up the flour without an argument. She can explain the broken axle immediately; no persuasion roll is required.

Orlo, a porter sheltering behind a stone, wants to retrieve a dropped keepsake. He follows a clear safe instruction and can carry the medicine. He is a person to protect, not a compulsory combat companion.

Ground. The cart is ten feet long with a five-foot gap on either side between its wheels and the clearing stones. Its body gives ordinary cover when the geometry supports it. The ditch is difficult footing but conceals someone carrying a small load. A loose flour sack lies near the animal’s approach; splitting it distracts with scent and dust rather than causing magical blindness.

Information. Nessa points out that the animal keeps sniffing the flour. Following its gaze reveals the spilled provisions without a check. The replacement pin fits, but the wheel must be lifted. A player can hold off the animal, help repair, carry the medicine out, bait it away or propose a different escape.

Repair. Nessa needs two uninterrupted opportunities to work after someone steadies the wheel. A character using their action to help completes one opportunity with her; a suitable tool or lever can remove the need to hold it. An attack forcing her away interrupts that opportunity, not earlier work. Count this openly as GM-adjudicated progress. Do not make it an invisible timer or grant extra combat actions.

People before property. If the player abandons the cart, Nessa can lead Orlo along the ditch while the player covers the retreat. The animal pursues accessible food rather than inexplicably hunting fleeing people. If no one helps, Nessa offers the flour and attempts that escape herself.

### Objectives

objective-1

### Approaches and branches

Bait with provisions: surrender the flour, move the people and medicine while the beast feeds, and resolve any uncertain close approach with the Ruleset.

Hold and repair: defend the wagon long enough to restore the wheel, then leave together.

Leave the load: carry only what is safe. Orlo’s keepsake can be recovered if the situation permits; losing it is a small personal cost, not a second quest.

### Consequences

Record whether Nessa, Orlo, the medicine and flour escape. Nessa pays the agreed amount if able; partial recovery earns gratitude even if the job loses money.

If the player made a promise to Orlo, resolve it in the aftermath. A saved keepsake becomes a tangible thank-you rather than an automatic companion recruitment.

All linked objective conditions are required, including the named closing event. Carry optional promises forward; they neither replace nor extend this ending.

### Prepared encounters

One encounter only. Solo level-one baseline: a hungry juvenile Rifthound, AC 12, HP 9, speed 40 ft, initiative +2; bite +3 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target, 1d4+1 piercing. This is an authored weaker adaptation of the referenced creature. It has no phase-step, regeneration, resistances or multiattack. Use start_combat_encounter_entities if combat begins, then resolve_adjudicated_creature_attack for its bite with these declared inputs. The first lunge targets exposed food or whoever blocks access. It retreats at 3 HP or when it can carry food clear. For a higher-level character or multiple combatants, choose and disclose an appropriate number or stronger referenced version before engagement; preserve the one encounter and objective instead of spawning surprise waves.

Read the selected party before committing opposition. The written encounter is a suggested baseline, not automatic level scaling. Resolve checks, attacks, damage, resources and combat turns through the admitted D&D SRD Ruleset; narrate only committed results. Preserve negotiation, surrender, retreat and established positions.

## The stalled crossing

Get the people and essential cargo away from a predator at the damaged wagon.

Character entry and scope. Recommended level 1–3; one player with zero to 2 optional companions. This is guidance, not an enforced level limit. The chosen character can accept the immediate invitation, negotiate terms or decline. Establish any needed local context openly without inventing prior player actions.

Nessa Rill, Guild driver: capable, embarrassed and direct. She wants everyone alive, then the medicine saved. She offers 10 gp for assistance and will give up the flour without an argument. She can explain the broken axle immediately; no persuasion roll is required.

Orlo, a porter sheltering behind a stone, wants to retrieve a dropped keepsake. He follows a clear safe instruction and can carry the medicine. He is a person to protect, not a compulsory combat companion.

Ground. The cart is ten feet long with a five-foot gap on either side between its wheels and the clearing stones. Its body gives ordinary cover when the geometry supports it. The ditch is difficult footing but conceals someone carrying a small load. A loose flour sack lies near the animal’s approach; splitting it distracts with scent and dust rather than causing magical blindness.

Information. Nessa points out that the animal keeps sniffing the flour. Following its gaze reveals the spilled provisions without a check. The replacement pin fits, but the wheel must be lifted. A player can hold off the animal, help repair, carry the medicine out, bait it away or propose a different escape.

Repair. Nessa needs two uninterrupted opportunities to work after someone steadies the wheel. Tone: Urgent, practical, hopeful survival

## Private truths and reveal conditions

## The stalled crossing

Get the people and essential cargo away from a predator at the damaged wagon.

Character entry and scope. Recommended level 1–3; one player with zero to 2 optional companions. This is guidance, not an enforced level limit. The chosen character can accept the immediate invitation, negotiate terms or decline. Establish any needed local context openly without inventing prior player actions.

Nessa Rill, Guild driver: capable, embarrassed and direct. She wants everyone alive, then the medicine saved. She offers 10 gp for assistance and will give up the flour without an argument. She can explain the broken axle immediately; no persuasion roll is required.

Orlo, a porter sheltering behind a stone, wants to retrieve a dropped keepsake. He follows a clear safe instruction and can carry the medicine. He is a person to protect, not a compulsory combat companion.

Ground. The cart is ten feet long with a five-foot gap on either side between its wheels and the clearing stones. Its body gives ordinary cover when the geometry supports it. The ditch is difficult footing but conceals someone carrying a small load. A loose flour sack lies near the animal’s approach; splitting it distracts with scent and dust rather than causing magical blindness.

Information. Nessa points out that the animal keeps sniffing the flour. Following its gaze reveals the spilled provisions without a check. The replacement pin fits, but the wheel must be lifted. A player can hold off the animal, help repair, carry the medicine out, bait it away or propose a different escape.

Repair. Nessa needs two uninterrupted opportunities to work after someone steadies the wheel. A character using their action to help completes one opportunity with her; a suitable tool or lever can remove the need to hold it. An attack forcing her away interrupts that opportunity, not earlier work. Count this openly as GM-adjudicated progress. Do not make it an invisible timer or grant extra combat actions.

People before property. If the player abandons the cart, Nessa can lead Orlo along the ditch while the player covers the retreat. The animal pursues accessible food rather than inexplicably hunting fleeing people. If no one helps, Nessa offers the flour and attempts that escape herself.

### Objectives

objective-1

### Approaches and branches

Bait with provisions: surrender the flour, move the people and medicine while the beast feeds, and resolve any uncertain close approach with the Ruleset.

Hold and repair: defend the wagon long enough to restore the wheel, then leave together.

Leave the load: carry only what is safe. Orlo’s keepsake can be recovered if the situation permits; losing it is a small personal cost, not a second quest.

### Consequences

Record whether Nessa, Orlo, the medicine and flour escape. Nessa pays the agreed amount if able; partial recovery earns gratitude even if the job loses money.

If the player made a promise to Orlo, resolve it in the aftermath. A saved keepsake becomes a tangible thank-you rather than an automatic companion recruitment.

All linked objective conditions are required, including the named closing event. Carry optional promises forward; they neither replace nor extend this ending.

### Prepared encounters

One encounter only. Solo level-one baseline: a hungry juvenile Rifthound, AC 12, HP 9, speed 40 ft, initiative +2; bite +3 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target, 1d4+1 piercing. This is an authored weaker adaptation of the referenced creature. It has no phase-step, regeneration, resistances or multiattack. Use start_combat_encounter_entities if combat begins, then resolve_adjudicated_creature_attack for its bite with these declared inputs. The first lunge targets exposed food or whoever blocks access. It retreats at 3 HP or when it can carry food clear. ## The stalled crossing

Get the people and essential cargo away from a predator at the damaged wagon.

Character entry and scope. Recommended level 1–3; one player with zero to 2 optional companions. This is guidance, not an enforced level limit. The chosen character can accept the immediate invitation, negotiate terms or decline. Establish any needed local context openly without inventing prior player actions.

Nessa Rill, Guild driver: capable, embarrassed and direct. She wants everyone alive, then the medicine saved. She offers 10 gp for assistance and will give up the flour without an argument. She can explain the broken axle immediately; no persuasion roll is required.

Orlo, a porter sheltering behind a stone, wants to retrieve a dropped keepsake. He follows a clear safe instruction and can carry the medicine. He is a person to protect, not a compulsory combat companion.

objective-1

Bait with provisions: surrender the flour, move the people and medicine while the beast feeds, and resolve any uncertain close approach with the Ruleset.

Hold and repair: defend the wagon long enough to restore the wheel, then leave together.

Leave the load: carry only what is safe. Orlo’s keepsake can be recovered if the situation permits; losing it is a small personal cost, not a second quest.

### Consequences

Record whether Nessa, Orlo, the medicine and flour escape. Nessa pays the agreed amount if able; partial recovery earns gratitude even if the job loses money.

If the player made a promise to Orlo, resolve it in the aftermath. A saved keepsake becomes a tangible thank-you rather than an automatic companion recruitment.

All linked objective conditions are required, including the named closing event. Carry optional promises forward; they neither replace nor extend this ending.

One encounter only. Solo level-one baseline: a hungry juvenile Rifthound, AC 12, HP 9, speed 40 ft, initiative +2; bite +3 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target, 1d4+1 piercing. This is an authored weaker adaptation of the referenced creature. It has no phase-step, regeneration, resistances or multiattack. planned_encounters: One encounter only. Solo level-one baseline: a hungry juvenile Rifthound, AC 12, HP 9, speed 40 ft, initiative +2; bite +3 to hit, reach 5 ft, one target, 1d4+1 piercing. This is an authored weaker adaptation of the referenced creature. It has no phase-step, regeneration, resistances or multiattack. Use start_combat_encounter_entities if combat begins, then resolve_adjudicated_creature_attack for its bite with these declared inputs. The first lunge targets exposed food or whoever blocks access. It retreats at 3 HP or when it can carry food clear. For a higher-level character or multiple combatants, choose and disclose an appropriate number or stronger referenced version before engagement; preserve the one encounter and objective instead of spawning surprise waves.
situations: Character entry and scope. Recommended level 1–3; one player with zero to 2 optional companions. This is guidance, not an enforced level limit. The chosen character can accept the immediate invitation, negotiate terms or decline. Establish any needed local context openly without inventing prior player actions.

Nessa Rill, Guild driver: capable, embarrassed and direct. She wants everyone alive, then the medicine saved. She offers 10 gp for assistance and will give up the flour without an argument. She can explain the broken axle immediately; no persuasion roll is required.

Orlo, a porter sheltering behind a stone, wants to retrieve a dropped keepsake. He follows a clear safe instruction and can carry the medicine. He is a person to protect, not a compulsory combat companion.

Ground. The cart is ten feet long with a five-foot gap on either side between its wheels and the clearing stones. Its body gives ordinary cover when the geometry supports it. The ditch is difficult footing but conceals someone carrying a small load. A loose flour sack lies near the animal’s approach; splitting it distracts with scent and dust rather than causing magical blindness.

Information. Nessa points out that the animal keeps sniffing the flour. Following its gaze reveals the spilled provisions without a check. The replacement pin fits, but the wheel must be lifted. A player can hold off the animal, help repair, carry the medicine out, bait it away or propose a different escape.

Repair. Nessa needs two uninterrupted opportunities to work after someone steadies the wheel. A character using their action to help completes one opportunity with her; a suitable tool or lever can remove the need to hold it. An attack forcing her away interrupts that opportunity, not earlier work. Count this openly as GM-adjudicated progress. Do not make it an invisible timer or grant extra combat actions.

People before property. If the player abandons the cart, Nessa can lead Orlo along the ditch while the player covers the retreat. The animal pursues accessible food rather than inexplicably hunting fleeing people. If no one helps, Nessa offers the flour and attempts that escape herself.

## The stalled crossing

Get the people and essential cargo away from a predator at the damaged wagon.

Character entry and scope. Recommended level 1–3; one player with zero to 2 optional companions. This is guidance, not an enforced level limit. The chosen character can accept the immediate invitation, negotiate terms or decline. Establish any needed local context openly without inventing prior player actions.

Nessa Rill, Guild driver: capable, embarrassed and direct. She wants everyone alive, then the medicine saved. She offers 10 gp for assistance and will give up the flour without an argument. She can explain the broken axle immediately; no persuasion roll is required.

Orlo, a porter sheltering behind a stone, wants to retrieve a dropped keepsake. He follows a clear safe instruction and can carry the medicine. He is a person to protect, not a compulsory combat companion.

Ground. The cart is ten feet long with a five-foot gap on either side between its wheels and the clearing stones. Its body gives ordinary cover when the geometry supports it. The ditch is difficult footing but conceals someone carrying a small load. A loose flour sack lies near the animal’s approach; splitting it distracts with scent and dust rather than causing magical blindness.

Information. Nessa points out that the animal keeps sniffing the flour. Following its gaze reveals the spilled provisions without a check. The replacement pin fits, but the wheel must be lifted. A player can hold off the animal, help repair, carry the medicine out, bait it away or propose a different escape.

Repair. Nessa needs two uninterrupted opportunities to work after someone steadies the wheel. A character using their action to help completes one opportunity with her; a suitable tool or lever can remove the need to hold it. An attack forcing her away interrupts that opportunity, not earlier work. Count this openly as GM-adjudicated progress. Do not make it an invisible timer or grant extra combat actions.

People before property. If the player abandons the cart, Nessa can lead Orlo along the ditch while the player covers the retreat. The animal pursues accessible food rather than inexplicably hunting fleeing people. If no one helps, Nessa offers the flour and attempts that escape herself.

Leave the load: carry only what is safe. Orlo’s keepsake can be recovered if the situation permits; losing it is a small personal cost, not a second quest.

### Consequences

Record whether Nessa, Orlo, the medicine and flour escape. Nessa pays the agreed amount if able; partial recovery earns gratitude even if the job loses money.

The medicine and flour are each recorded as carried out, left at the wagon, consumed or lost through play. Record the wagon and any keepsake actually recovered; rescuing property is not required after the people are safe.

Closing event: on safe ground Nessa responds to the actual rescue and losses and settles the agreed assistance payment if able. If she was lost, Orlo or the receiving Guild contact takes the report instead. No additional delivery adventure is required.

## Failure and withdrawal

Use the explicit failed-attempt outcome and closing report in the current objective. An intention to withdraw, an unrelated side task or delegation alone does not satisfy it. An early departure leaves unplayed later objectives unfinished.

Resolve defeat, unconsciousness, death and recovery under the selected Ruleset and agreed boundaries; no scripted rescue cancels committed results.

## Optional continuation

Only after resolving this adventure, ask whether the player wants to pursue a surviving relationship or optional lead. The ending does not depend on accepting.
